name: Cincinnati Art Week
tagline: A CELEBRATION OF ART & IDEAS & CREATIVE COMMUNITY
description:
From October 3–10 2026, Cincinnati Art Week brings exhibitions, pop-up galleries, social gatherings, and special programming to Over-the-Rhine.

Cincinnati is an art city. It’s home to one of the Midwest's most vibrant creative communities. Cincinnati Art Week invites you to experience it.

Designed by artists, the week connects residents and visitors with exhibitions, conversations, creative experiences, public programming and the people shaping Cincinnati’s cultural landscape.

Cincinnati Art Week begins in Over-the-Rhine and grows from there. Each year, we'll expand into new neighborhoods, strengthening connections between artists, organizations, and the communities they call home.
creators_note:
A note from the
creators of
Cincinnati Art Week

From October 3–10, 2026, Cincinnati Art Week (CAW) debuts as a new annual celebration of connection, culture, and creativity.

CAW is created by Cincy Nice in partnership with No Standing and community partners. More than a week of exhibitions, Cincinnati Art Week is an invitation to experience the city through the people making it.

It’s born from admiration for our artist community and a shared commitment to:

• Honor who's already here and invest in their potential

• Welcome bold ideas and the people who carry them

• Create space for connection, collaboration, & what's next

We believe it's merrier with more, that good ideas like company, and the magic happens when we unite.

This is gonna be an ambitious year one (we’re gonna keep it real). We're intentionally focused on building a strong foundation to build upon.

We'd love your support as we bring Cincinnati Art Week to life. Whether you're a sponsor, artist, volunteer, business owner, neighbor, or simply curious, there's a place for you here. Please don't hesitate to get in touch, share an idea, or attend an upcoming event. We can’t wait to connect.

We're going for it. Let's go together and see what's possible.

To who’s already here!
And to what’s next!

With anticipation,

the Cincinnati Art Week team

plans_announced: During the inaugural Cincinnati Art Week, visitors can expect two self-guided Art Walks through Over-the-Rhine; six to eight vacant storefronts transformed into exhibitions, pop-up galleries and experiences through a partnership with developers 3CDC, Urban Sites and Model Group; featured projects from emerging, established and visiting artists; a central Cincinnati Art Week hub for creative gatherings and social experiences; artist talks, demonstrations and community conversations; opportunities to discover local artists, galleries and creative spaces; and neighborhood partnerships and community programming.
visitor_tip: So what’s the best way to experience Cincinnati Art Week? Begin at the Welcome Center at 1600 Race St., the main hub for the week. There, you can ask questions, grab a map and pick up merch before heading out to explore.
visitcincy_description: Discover Cincinnati’s creative side during Cincinnati Art Week, an annual celebration of art, ideas and creativity taking place Oct. 3-10, 2026, in Over-the-Rhine. Presented by ArtsWave and Fifth Third, the event is a project by Cincy Nice in partnership with No Standing. Throughout the week, storefronts and unexpected spaces across the neighborhood will transform into temporary galleries and gathering places. Visitors can view exhibitions, meet artists, shop original work and take part in special programming, including artist-led events, the Cincinnati Art Week Art Market, special projects and after-dark experiences. Follow the map, find a new favorite piece or connect with the people shaping Cincinnati’s creative scene. With free events and experiences throughout Over-the-Rhine, there’s plenty to see and do. Come explore Over-the-Rhine, discover new work and experience Cincinnati’s creative scene during this weeklong celebration.

cincy-nice.who_we_are: Cincy Nice is a Cultural Strategy & Civic Experience Studio based in Cincinnati, Ohio. Our work lives at the intersection of culture, participation, and possibility.
cincy-nice.team: Cincy Nice is led by co-founders Destinee and William Thomas. Together, our work spans public art, citywide festivals, community engagement, partnerships, and neighborhood initiatives across Cincinnati.
cincy-nice.how_we_work: Still Smiling. It's more than a mantra. It's our theory of change. We believe the most meaningful change begins with human connection.
cincy-nice.story: In the years that followed, we hosted dinners for strangers, produced the nation’s largest light festival (twice), supported artists, activated public spaces, built partnerships, and spent countless hours helping people gather around ideas worth pursuing.

projects.title: Our Tables | Public Repair
projects.text:
Our Tables

Turning a moment of unrest into a shared table.

In the summer of 2020, Cincinnati was hurting. Windows were boarded, tensions were high, and people were searching for a way to move forward.

Created on Juneteenth by Cincy Nice alongside a coalition of Black artists, organizers, activists, and cultural leaders, the project transformed boarded-up window art from Over-the-Rhine businesses into long communal tables on Main Street. What had been used as a barrier became an invitation.

projects.title: More Free 2020 | Civic Participation
projects.text:
MORE FREE 2020

A little more joy. A little more action. A little more free.

Launched during one of the most uncertain years in recent memory, More Free was a community movement built around a simple idea: participation should feel hopeful.

Through creative campaigns, neighborhood activations, mutual aid, and a pop-up storefront “voter resource” community hub, we encouraged people to connect, contribute, and take action together. Along the way, we helped hundreds get registered to vote, launched Cincinnati's first free fridge and created a platform that blended civic engagement with creativity, generosity, and joy.

projects.title: Social House | A Welcoming Space
projects.text:
Cincy Nice Social House

Expanding visibility, connection, and creative exchange during BLINK Cincinnati.

During BLINK 2019 and again in BLINK 2022, we transformed retail space into a vibrant and ephemeral cultural hub and lounge co-created by 45+ artists and collaborators.

Alongside creating a welcoming gathering space, the project provided increased visibility for Black artists, creatives, and cultural leaders during one of Cincinnati's largest cultural events. More than 1,100 people participated over three days, helping spark relationships, collaborations, and ideas that continue to influence our work today.

projects.title: Mural Project | Imagine 876 x Five Points Alley
projects.text:
ADDING ART TO DEFINE SPACE AND CREATE A FEELING OF JOY, WELCOMENESS, AND HOPE

5 POINTS ALLEY MURAL BY IMAGINE 876

In our continued effort to add vibrancy and establish 5 Points Alley as a lasting creative, community gathering space for Walnut Hills, Cincy Nice commissioned Nepalese artist Imagine 876 to create a large scale mural on the back exterior of the The Dillard Center building.

Since late 2020, Cincy Nice has partnered with the Walnut Hills Redevelopment Foundation to manage and program Five Points Alley as a community gathering space.

projects.title: Still Smiling Fest | A Celebration of Joy
projects.text:
stillsmilingfest.com

WOW. YOUR SMILE SHINES SO BRIGHT.

The first Still Smiling Fest festival invited attendees to join Cincy Nice in Five Points Alley for a moment of shared joy as we collectively shook off the trying times of the past two years, and welcomed a new era of good times in.

The two-night event transformed Walnut Hill's’ Five Points Alley community courtyard into a happy oasis featuring national music acts with headliners including grammy-awarding artist Mýa and Cincinnati-native Sudan Archives with emerging local music acts including Soul Criminals, Siri Imani, Lauren Eylise and more + live art making, and local food vendors.

projects.title: Soul Plates | Passing the Culture
projects.text:
soulplates.org

CREATING THE TOGETHERNESS OF A SHARED MEAL VIRTUALLY THROUGH SMELL, TASTE, SOUND & STORYTELLING.

By December 2020, everyone was feeling the weight of the on-going COVID pandemic and longing to gather around the table like holidays past. We set out to find a way to connect with one another, as we would around the dinner table, in what had become a virtual world.

To do this, we invited guests to travel deeper into the diverse flavors and traditions that define cultures, communities and individuals by reflecting on the idea of “soul food” and our connection to cooking and eating as a form of resistance, an act of joy, an expression of love—an essential part of who we are at our core.

projects.title: 5 Points Alley | Back to Community
projects.text:
fivepointsalley.org | @5pointsalley

A NEW CREATIVE COMMUNITY COURTYARD EMERGES.

Tucked away, nestled in the heart of Walnut Hills, 5 Points Alley is a central meeting point for all that the neighborhood has to offer. It is our community courtyard, a place where local residents, businesses & visitors come together to form friendships, share smiles, and spark connections.

We designed and programmed 5 Points Alley with intentionality and respect for our shared goal of creating a black-forward community space where joyful experiences thrive and all who enter feel a sense of belonging.
